prompt: Find suspicious card transactions when only a handful of past fraud cases were ever labeled.
tells: only a handful of past fraud cases were ever labeled
why: Model normal behavior and flag what doesn't fit (isolation forest, autoencoders).
trap: Supervised models need many labeled examples of the rare class.

prompt: Alert when a factory machine's vibration readings look unusual compared with its normal operation.
tells: look unusual compared with its normal operation
why: Learn the normal range and alert on deviations.
trap: Forecasting is a tool for it, but the goal is spotting the unusual.

prompt: Flag account logins that are out of character for that user: new country, odd hour, unusual device.
tells: out of character for that user
why: Per-user baselines, then score how far a login deviates.
trap: Clustering groups users; this asks what's abnormal for one user.

prompt: Automatically detect sudden spikes or drops across 5,000 business metrics without hand-set thresholds.
why: Learn each metric's normal behavior (with seasonality) and flag outliers.
trap: A/B tests compare variants; they don't watch metrics.

prompt: Spot unusual network traffic that might be an intrusion, when attackers keep changing tactics and labeled attacks are scarce.
why: Model normal traffic and flag deviations; new attacks won't match old labels anyway.
trap: A classifier only catches attack types it was trained on.

prompt: A factory camera sees thousands of good parts a day and only a few defects a month. Flag parts that look different from normal.
tells: only a few defects a month
why: Train on good parts only (for example an autoencoder) and flag high reconstruction error.
trap: Too few defects to train a reliable classifier.

prompt: Find expense claims that look unusual for that employee's role and history, for auditors to review.
tells: look unusual for that employee's role and history
why: Compare each claim to its peer and personal baseline and surface outliers.
trap: Clustering groups employees; the goal is flagging odd claims.

prompt: An alert on checkout volume fires every Sunday night, when traffic is always low, while real drops on busy weekdays go unnoticed.
tells: real drops on busy weekdays go unnoticed
why: The detector needs a seasonal baseline (expected value for this hour and weekday), not a fixed threshold.
trap: Forecasting provides the baseline, but the task is detecting deviations from it.
